Who We Are

Vermeer equips customers doing important work around the world. We are global, driven by innovation and growing. The equipment we make manages natural resources, connects people and feeds and fuels communities. We live out a caring culture, we demonstrate agility, we keep a focus on customers and are stewards of our resources. These beliefs drive our culture, determine how we treat others and steer our business.

Work Shift

1 - First Shift

Job Summary

As an IT Software Engineer Intern at Vermeer, you will gain hands‑on experience designing and supporting modern software solutions that strengthen business operations across the organization. You’ll collaborate with experienced engineers, practice foundational development concepts, and contribute to real product enhancements while building skills in cloud technologies, application development, and team‑based Agile delivery.

What You’ll Do:

1. Contribute to software development tasks using object‑oriented programming concepts and languages such as C#, .NET, JavaScript, or TypeScript. You will assist in writing clean, maintainable code that supports application functionality and user experience.

2. Support the creation and testing of Representational State Transfer (RESTful) Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) and cloud services hosted within Microsoft Azure. This includes practicing secure coding and basic debugging techniques.

3. Participate in source control processes and introductory Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) workflows, using automated build and test activities under the guidance of senior developers.

4. Assist in working with relational and non‑relational databases to retrieve, validate, and prepare data that supports application features and integrations.

5. Join Agile ceremonies such as sprint planning, standups, and retrospectives to gain experience with iterative development and collaborative team delivery.

6. Document findings, update reference materials, and help troubleshoot simple issues to support the overall software development lifecycle.

7. Explore emerging technologies and modern engineering practices while applying classroom learning to real‑world scenarios.

What We’re Looking For:

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field.

- Exposure to web development or application frameworks using languages such as C#, .NET, JavaScript, or TypeScript through coursework or project work.

- Familiarity with RESTful APIs, cloud concepts, or CI/CD basics, with willingness to strengthen these skills through hands‑on practice.

- Understanding of standard data formats, including JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) and Extensible Markup Language (XML).

- Strong curiosity, initiative, and willingness to learn new tools and approaches in a collaborative environment.

- Clear communication skills, professionalism, and ability to work productively with technical and nontechnical partners.

- Interest in problem‑solving and continuous learning within modern software engineering disciplines.

Travel:

- No travel required of this position.

Work Location

ONSITE: A team member’s day-to-day work is best done on a Vermeer campus. If work content can be occasionally completed at an offsite location, discuss potential arrangements with your manager.

Equal Opportunity Employer

At Vermeer Corporation, we believe in the value of your unique identity, background, and experiences. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status or any other status protected by the law. Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation due to a disability at any stage of the employment application process should contact Team Member Solutions at (641) 621-8767 or at hr@vermeer.com.

Why Patients Need You

At Pfizer, we apply science and our global resources to bring therapies to people that extend and significantly improve their lives. We strive to set the standard for quality, safety, and value in the discovery, development, and manufacture of health care products. Our global portfolio includes medicines and vaccines as well as many of the world's best-known consumer health care products. Every day, Pfizer colleagues work across developed and emerging markets to advance wellness, prevention, treatments, and cures that challenge the most feared diseases of our time. Consistent with our responsibility as one of the world's premier innovative biopharmaceutical companies, we collaborate with health care providers, governments, and local communities to support and expand access to reliable, affordable health care around the world. For more than 170 years, Pfizer has worked to make a difference for all who rely on us.

What You Will Achieve

Pfizer's Marketing team operates across various therapeutic areas, focusing on innovative and impactful strategies. They are tasked with effectively positioning Pfizer's products in the competitive pharmaceutical market. This involves developing disease-area strategies, planning for new products, preparing and executing brand launches, and continuously refining brand positioning, messaging, and promotions. Marketers conduct thorough market and product research pre-launch to assess a product's value proposition for patients, prescribers, and payers, ensuring optimal market positioning. Post-launch, they adapt product positioning to maximize patient value.

Jumpstart your marketing career with Pfizer's Marketing Summer Associate role, a gateway to our dynamic two-year Marketing Rotational Program. Immerse yourself in a marketing team, tackle real-world commercial projects, and explore the pharmaceutical industry's multifaceted areas. Connect and learn from your peers, brand managers, and senior leaders throughout the summer. Benefit from personalized guidance with a senior leader advisor, mentor, and buddy system. Stand out as a high performer and secure a full-time spot in the Rotational Program, where you'll gain diverse experience across business units and marketing functions. This program is your fast track to building a solid foundation in pharmaceutical marketing and becoming a future leader at Pfizer.

Pharmaceutical marketing, while complex and continuously evolving, is essential for healthcare advancement. It bridges information gaps, accelerates patient care, and supports research and development, making its impact felt across the entire healthcare landscape.

What Does the Program Entail?

- A 10-week immersive, practical marketing project with well-defined objectives

- Information sessions and networking with senior leaders and colleagues

- Team building, philanthropic and professional networking events

- Mid and end-of-summer performance reviews

- Final project presentation sessions

Types of Projects:

- US Marketing: Brand Strategy, Tactical Asset Creation & Execution, Promotional Material Development

- Global Marketing: Global Brand Strategy, Product Launch, Above-Brand Strategy, Commercial Development

- Chief Marketing Office: Commercial Analytics & AI, Global Media, Growth & Performance Marketing, Customer Engagement Platforms & Technology

​Qualifications

Must Have

- Bachelor’s degree

- Enrolled in a Full-Time MBA program

- 1st year MBA student graduating in Spring 2028

- At least 3 years of full-time work experience

- Demonstrated interest in pharmaceutical and/or healthcare​

- Ability to break down and solve problems through quantitative thinking and analysis

- Ability to work collaboratively in a team and create an inclusive environment with people at all levels of an organization

- Demonstrated leadership qualities and high level of Emotional Intelligence

- Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills

​Nice to Have

- MBA emphasis in Marketing, Healthcare Management, Consulting and/or Strategy

- Previous consulting, pharmaceutical, or healthcare experience

Other Job Details

- Last Date to Apply: November 30, 2026 11:59pm ET

- Must be immediately authorized to work in the U.S. on a permanent or indefinitely renewable basis without employer’s sponsorship. Pfizer will be unable to provide any employment visa or green card sponsorship for this position. Pfizer is an Equal Opportunity and E-Verify employer.

- Work Location Assignment: MBA Summer Associates work out of Pfizer’s New York Headquarters in Hudson Yards, Manhattan and will be expected to come into the office 4 days a week to connect and innovate with their team face-to-face.

- This opportunity is meant for the Summer of 2027.

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever.

At Micron, the DRAM Design organization develops industry-leading memory solutions that span technology development, advanced circuit design, product engineering, system validation, and manufacturing enablement. Teams collaborate globally to deliver innovative memory products that meet demanding requirements for performance, quality, reliability, and time-to-market.

As an Intern DRAM Design Engineer, you will contribute to the design, analysis, verification, and optimization of digital, analog, and mixed-signal circuits used in next-generation memory products. You will work closely with design, verification, product engineering, test, process integration, assembly, and marketing teams to support new product development and manufacturability initiatives. This role also provides opportunities to apply Artificial Intelligence and AI Assisted methodologies to improve design workflows, automation, and design quality.

Responsibilities

- Play a key role in the development of new memory products through circuit build, layout, optimization, and validation of Memory, Logic, and Analog circuits.
- Support physical design activities including parasitic modeling, floor-planning, placement, routing, reticle experiments, tape-out revisions, and design verification using industry-standard simulation tools.
- Collaborate with global design, verification, product engineering, test, process integration, assembly, and marketing teams to improve manufacturability, quality, and product performance.
- Proactively engage with CAD, modeling, standards, and verification teams to improve design methodologies and overall design quality.
- Develop AI Assisted software tools and leverage Artificial Intelligence to enhance design methodologies, workflow automation, engineering productivity, and design quality.

Minimum Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering or Computer Engineering.
- Must be continuing academic studies through at least Fall 2027 and not graduate before Fall 2027.
- Coursework, academic projects, or research experience in digital design, analog design, semiconductor devices, VLSI, computer architecture, or related areas.
- Strong problem-solving, analytical, and communication skills with the ability to work effectively both independently and within team environments.
- Experience preparing and presenting technical findings through reports, presentations, or project evaluations.

Preferred Qualifications

- Experience with circuit simulation, verification, modeling, or industry-standard EDA tools.
- Understanding of semiconductor manufacturing, memory architecture, DRAM design concepts, or integrated circuit development.
- Familiarity with physical design concepts including floor-planning, placement, routing, parasitic extraction, or layout optimization.
- Experience Applying AI, Using AI, or Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to improve engineering workflows, automation, software development, or technical analysis.
- Exposure to AI Assisted tools, Generative AI, Agentic AI, LLMs, or AI-Enabled software solutions for engineering productivity and design optimization.

About Us:

Perpay is a certified B Corp and Philadelphia’s most impactful growth-stage startup. We are driven by a mission to significantly improve the financial stability of everyday Americans. For the past decade, we have established strong product-market fit and a profitable, efficient operating model across a suite of products, positioning Perpay as the premier financial partner for consumers with subprime credit.

With over 500,000 customers who have utilized more than $1 billion in spending power, we are at a pivotal moment. We are scaling our operations, building new offerings, and deepening our impact. We are looking for teammates eager to join us on this journey.

Our venture partners include First Round Capital and L Catterton.

Products we’ve built to make an impact:

- Perpay Marketplace: Combines interest-free payments and modern e-commerce to reduce cost of ownership and promote healthy repayment behavior.

- Perpay+: Leverages Marketplace repayment history to help members monitor and build credit with all 3 credit bureaus.

- Perpay Credit Card: Expands access to the flexibility and benefits of a World Mastercard by removing common barriers like high security deposits and low approval odds.

Our team thrives on in-person collaboration, operating from our unique center-city Philadelphia office. This comfortable "home away from home" space offers river views and fosters rapid product development, strong relationships, and career growth. The energy from achieving big wins is palpable here. While we primarily work in the office, we offer sensible flexibility for personal needs, such as sick children or urgent errands, and coordinate official remote weeks around major holidays. If you are passionate about a meaningful mission, collaboration, equity, and generous perks, Perpay is the best place to be in Philadelphia right now.

About the Role:

Our data team is organized across three groups: Data Engineering, Data Science, and Strategic Analytics. Data Engineering owns the warehouse, the orchestration layer, and the pipelines that move data from our operational systems to everyone who depends on it. This year, with the credit portfolio scaling and our modeling needs getting heavier, focus areas include real-time event ingestion, the risk decisioning service redesign, AI-agent data access on Redshift Serverless, ERP/EDI standardization with Finance and Accounting, and AI-assisted workflows across the engineering lifecycle.

As a Data Engineering intern, your main responsibility is to learn, but you'll learn it by doing real work. During the summer of 2027, you'll build data pipelines, help design tools and infrastructure for analyzing large volumes of data, and work through real data warehousing problems alongside the team that owns them. You'll partner directly with stakeholders across Risk, Commerce, Marketing, Ops, and Finance, and get hands-on with our full stack, which includes AWS (Redshift, Glue, ECS, DMS), Fivetran, Airflow, DataHub, Terraform, Python, and SQL.

Our greatest strength is our people, and we’d love for you to be one of them!

What to Expect from the Internship:

Within your first week, you'll:

- Introduce yourself on Slack and meet your team.

- Get oriented in the warehouse, walk through our most-used pipelines with the rest of the team, and read enough of the codebase to start asking useful questions.

Within your first month, you'll:

- Get fluent enough in our Airflow setup and Redshift conventions to navigate the codebase independently.

- Scope your first real project with a mentor, including the design decisions and trade-offs involved.

- Ship your first commit. It could be a bug fix, a documentation update, or a small improvement.

By the end of your internship, you'll:

- Have shipped a pipeline, tool, or infrastructure improvement that the team relies on after you're gone.

- Have presented your work to the broader team, and walked away with a real sense of what production data engineering looks like day to day.

- Have met with various business owners across the company to build your network and get a feel for how a data team fits into a fast-paced startup.

What You’ll Bring:

- Currently enrolled in or will receive a Master's in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Management, Information Systems, Mathematics, or an equivalent technical discipline, with an expected graduation date between winter 2027 – summer 2028, or equivalent relevant experience.

- Experience using SQL for acquiring and transforming data.

- Experience with database and/or data warehouse operations.

- Exposure to third-party APIs.

- Experience with object-oriented programming languages (Python preferred)

Bonus:

- Previous work experience in a technical field

- Exposure to open-source data tooling and cloud computing systems

- Understanding of data types and storage paradigms

Hey, we know not everybody checks all the boxes, so if you’re interested, please apply because you could be just what we’re looking for!

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Ground Systems Deployment Team

The Ground Systems Deployment and Construction team is responsible for turning bare ground into functional drone charging sites! We’re a broad, cross-functional team with skills across civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, and construction engineering with a mandate to deliver world-class construction execution with zero issues in the first 30 days, on-time and on-budget, using scalable, cost-optimized, and serviceable designs.

The Role

As a Civil/Structural Engineer Intern on the Ground Systems Deployment team, you will support the rollout of Zipline’s site infrastructure across multiple metros and help shape how UAS infrastructure integrates with the built environment—not just for Zipline, but for our customers and the industry as a whole.

You will contribute to developing standards for charging sites and support the structural engineering of ground systems hardware and site infrastructure needed to secure permits and approvals for new Zipline sites.

You will work closely with cross-functional teams, including Real Estate & Development, Systems Engineering, and Tower Engineering, to ensure that site layouts and infrastructure meet Zipline’s engineering requirements as well as applicable municipal codes and permitting standards.

This position is based at our headquarters in South San Francisco.

What You'll Do

- Support the civil and structural design of new Zipline sites, including charging infrastructure, foundations, equipment pads, and other ground-system elements.

- Perform structural calculations and help develop drawings and design documentation that support permitting, construction, and site deployment.

- Help create and improve reusable design standards for charging sites and ground-system hardware, then adapt those standards to real-world site constraints.

- Support permitting and regulatory reviews by helping address comments and coordinate with municipalities, inspectors, consultants, and other external partners.

- Collaborate with teams across Real Estate & Development, Systems Engineering, Tower Engineering, construction, and deployment to understand how engineering decisions affect site layout, constructability, and operations.

- Evaluate site-specific engineering challenges and develop practical solutions that improve safety, constructability, cost, and speed of deployment.

- Gain hands-on experience taking infrastructure from early site concepts through permitting and construction, while learning how civil and structural engineering is applied to a rapidly scaling UAS network.

What You'll Bring

- You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies in Civil or Structural Engineering. Master's and PhD students are also eligible.

- Proficiency in Bluebeam and drafting software such as AutoCAD or Revit.

- Excellent communications and problem solving skills.

- Bonus: Experience working with building codes and developing site plans.

- The individual will be based at Zipline’s headquarters in San Francisco, with possible travel to the DWF area in Texas.

- An open mind to help us bring Zipline’s service to new and existing customers!

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September).

The hourly rate for this internship is $44 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organizations around the world use data. You'll create features used by research scientists, aerospace engineers, intelligence analysts, and economic forecasters in countries around the world. Palantir's Product Development organization is made up of small teams of Software Engineers, each focusing on a specific aspect of a product. For example, you might join a team that builds a Foundry front-end application, or a component of the Gotham release infrastructure. We encourage communication and collaboration among teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll also have the opportunity to learn about other business areas.

Core Responsibilities

As a Software Engineer, you are involved throughout the product lifecycle - from idea generation, design, and prototyping, to execution and shipping, all while also being paired with a mentor dedicated to your growth and success. You'll collaborate closely with technical and non-technical counterparts to understand our customers' problems and build products that tackle them. One of the most effective ways to understand what our users need is to meet them. You may receive an opportunity to tour the assembly line at an auto-manufacturer or join a counter-terror analyst at their desk to really understand their mission and difficulties.

• Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end in spite of obstacles we may encounter.

• Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other Software Engineers, Product Managers, Designers and Product Reliability Engineers. Technologies We Use

It doesn’t matter what languages you know when you join us; what matters is that you can write clean, effective code and learn new languages quickly. Our software is constantly evolving, so we need engineers who can do the same. Alongside peers that bring diverse experience - whether you’re a former university Teaching Assistant, switched to computer science recently, or are a hackathon enthusiast — you'll build your skills to apply the best technology to solve a given problem. Right now, we use:

• A variety of languages, including Java and Go for backend and Typescript for frontend

• Open-source technologies like Cassandra, Spark, Elasticsearch, React, and Redux

• Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub

- Ability to communicate and collaborate with a variety of individuals, including engineers, users and non-technical team members.

- Willingness to learn and make decisions independently, and the ability to ask questions effectively.

- Engineering background in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, and Physics.

- Familiarity with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools.

Job Description

Ready to make your mark in the world of data governance? Spend an unforgettable summer at Invesco alongside a select group of driven students. Our 9-week Summer Internship Program offers you the opportunity to work within our Corporate Functions Data Office, supporting initiatives that improve how data is governed, understood, and used across Finance, HR, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, and Risk.

As part of our Summer Internship Program cohort, you’ll participate in orientation, networking events, development workshops, and volunteer activities. You’ll work side by side with talented teams to learn about the business and contribute to meaningful initiatives that support data governance, data quality, reporting and process improvement across Corporate Functions.

If you enjoy analyzing data, improving processes, and turning information into clear insights, this role offers a unique opportunity to apply your skills in a dynamic, cross-functional environment. You’ll support initiatives that strengthen data governance, improve data quality, and help Corporate Functions use data more effectively.

Here’s the best part: crush your internship, and you could be eligible for a full-time offer to join our Early Career Program after graduation!

What You’ll Do

Support data governance initiatives across Corporate Functions:

- Help maintain inventories of critical data elements, data owners, data stewards, and key business processes

- Support preparation of materials for data governance meetings, working groups, and stakeholder updates

Assist with data quality and metadata activities:

- Analyze datasets to identify completeness, consistency, or accuracy issues

- Help document data definitions, business rules, lineage, and usage for key Corporate Function data

- Support data quality issue tracking by organizing findings, actions, owners, and status updates

Contribute to reporting, dashboards, and process improvement:

- Create or update dashboards, trackers, and summary reports to monitor data governance progress and key metrics

- Map current-state processes and help identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate recurring activities

- Assist with preparing executive-ready summaries, presentations, and visual materials that communicate insights clearly

Support cross-functional projects and research:

- Research leading practices in data governance, data management, AI readiness, and regulatory expectations

- Partner with team members across Corporate Functions to gather information, validate documentation, and support project deliverables

- Assist with ad hoc projects related to data governance, data quality, master data, controls, or transformation initiatives

- Access to Finance Leadership – Connect with finance leaders throughout the summer and gain insight into how strategic decisions are made across the business

Full time

We are pleased that you are interested in exploring opportunities to join RFCUNY.

OFFICE OF SR. UNIV DEAN FOR ACADEMIC AFFAIRS

Description

The City University of New York (CUNY) is the nation’s largest urban public university and serves 235,000 degree- seeking students and 150,000 non-degree students across 25 campuses. 77% are students of color. CUNY's core mandate is to provide a high-quality, affordable education to all New Yorkers. Guided by CUNY’s seven-year strategic plan, CUNY Lifting NY, to achieve this mission, it is imperative that CUNY students have access to high quality work‐based learning experiences that allow them to gain and demonstrate skills, experience real‐world applications, and directly launch their careers.

The CUNY Office of Careers & Industry Partnerships (OCIP) reports to the Chancellor and the University Provost and is responsible for mobilizing the university’s unparalleled scale, assets, and diverse talent to fuel inclusive economic prosperity and is dedicated to the mission of connecting academic pursuits with career competitiveness. OCIP works closely with industry to understand the skills required for the most in-demand jobs and trains City University of New York (CUNY) students in those skills to prepare them for early and sustained career success.

GENERAL DESCRIPTION

The Office of Career and Internship Programs seeks a collaborative and results-driven professional to lead and expand CUNY’s public sector internship initiatives.

Reporting to the Senior Director of Career Development and Internships, the Director will lead the development and growth of university-wide internship programs in partnership with New York City and State agencies. This role will focus on scaling employer partnerships, expanding paid internship opportunities for CUNY students, and strengthening pathways to public sector careers. The Director will work closely with campuses, government partners, and other stakeholders to align programs with workforce needs and increase access to high-quality, career-connected learning experiences.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership and Program Development

• Lead the design, expansion, and evaluation of innovative paid work-based learning initiatives aligned with institutional priorities, labor market trends, employer workforce needs, and student

success goals. • Establish program goals, performance metrics, operational standards, and annual work plans to measure program effectiveness and ensure continuous improvement.

• Provide leadership, supervision, coaching, and professional development to program managers and staff, establishing performance expectations, monitoring progress toward departmental goals, and fostering a collaborative, inclusive, and student-centered work environment.

• Develop, cultivate, and sustain strategic partnerships with government agencies, employers, academic departments, career services, faculty, campus leadership, and university administrators to integrate internships and experiential learning into academic pathways and increase student participation.

• Increase the number of employer partners through new partnerships and funding opportunities that support program growth and sustainability.

Program Operations, Administration, and Performance Management

• Direct the day-to-day administration of multiple internship and experiential learning programs, ensuring effective program delivery, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and high-quality student experiences.

• Create and manage program budgets, fiscal planning, contracts, and financial reporting, coordinating with university and external fiscal partners to ensure compliance, and adherence to grant and funding agency requirements.

• Lead the collection, analysis, and develop reporting of program data to evaluate performance, measure student and employer outcomes, assess return on investment, and identify opportunities for operational and programmatic improvement.

• Represent senior leadership in internal and external meetings as assigned, providing leadership continuity and strategic support during leadership absences.

• Perform other related duties and special projects as needed.

The Advanced Strategies & Research Technology Team in Fidelity’s Asset Management organization is an embedded team focused on unlocking the potential of new technologies, techniques and datasets, to assist our Investment Professionals in generating alpha for our investment products and customers.

The role is ideal for a skilled technical leader with strong design, collaboration and influencing skills.

Ideally the candidate is a full stack, but this role will be primarily focused on processing and generating Analytics from structured and unstructured datasets with the ability of parallel processing potentially in the cloud.

The ideal candidate with have a strong technology background with a demonstrated ability to quickly adapt to new technologies, a go-getter, a proven ability to work with quantitative concepts and data, and a solid understanding and experience with the investment management business.

The Vision of the team is to build a best-in-class platform for alternative data and the Mission is to provide the Right Data to the Right People at the Right Time with the Right Quality and Right Coverage.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

The Role

Every Zipline market grows differently. Customer behavior, commercial priorities, competition, partnerships, and local opportunities vary from city to city. We're looking for a Commercial Strategy & Operations Intern to help turn those local realities into clear priorities, better decisions, and measurable market growth.

You'll support the team responsible for understanding how your market is performing and where we can improve. You'll work with data, build analyses and reporting, contribute to planning, and help make sure cross-functional teams are aligned on the work that matters most. Success means helping the organization move faster, operate more effectively, and identify opportunities to improve customer, merchant, and market performance.

You'll partner closely with Commercial, Operations, Marketing, Analytics, Community Engagement, and other teams across the organization. You'll learn how a fast-growing marketplace business works while gaining hands-on experience solving ambiguous problems and translating insights into action.

What You'll Do

- Support weekly and monthly business reviews by pulling data, analyzing performance, and turning findings into clear takeaways and actions.

- Build and maintain reporting on key customer, merchant, commercial, and ops metrics.

- Analyze customer behavior, merchant performance, market trends, and operational data to identify opportunities and risks.

- Help develop business cases, forecasts, and recommendations for growth and operational initiatives.

- Partner with cross-functional teams to coordinate priorities, document decisions, track action items, and follow up on execution.

- Improve processes, templates, and operating rhythms that help teams plan and execute more effectively.

- Research competitors, local market dynamics, and emerging opportunities to inform commercial strategy.

- Prepare concise presentations and ad hoc analyses for leadership and partner teams.

- Own a defined commercial strategy or operations project from problem framing and analysis through recommendation and implementation support.

What You'll Bring

- Must have completed the second year of a bachelor's degree in business, economics, finance, data analytics, engineering, marketing, or a related field. Master’s are also eligible.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down complex questions and communicate the answer clearly

- Proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets; experience with SQL, dashboards, or other data tools is a plus.

- Strong attention to detail and the ability to organize multiple projects, deadlines, and stakeholders.

- Clear written and verbal communication skills, with comfort presenting findings and recommendations.

- Curiosity about how businesses grow and how strong operating practices turn strategy into results.

- A proactive, collaborative approach and willingness to take ownership in a fast-moving environment.

- Prior internship, campus leadership, project, or work experience involving analysis, operations, strategy, or cross-functional collaboration is a plus.

- Must be able to work onsite and travel frequently throughout Austin, Texas, San Antonio, Texas, Houston, Texas or Phoenix, Arizona. Requires transportation (not company provided) and the ability to independently travel to operational sites, events, communities, and partner locations as needed.

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our Dallas, Texas, Austin, Texas, Los Angeles, California OR Phoenix, Arizona office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns (May/June - August/September). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

About H3X Technologies

H3X is building America's advanced electric motor company, powering next-generation platforms in aerospace, defense, and marine. Our integrated motor drives deliver 12+ kW/kg, roughly 3x the power density of competing solutions. We're now scaling to megawatt-class systems, with customers working on everything from supersonic aircraft to turbine power generation for AI datacenters.

Our team brings together engineers and operators from aerospace, defense, and motorsports, with deep expertise in electric machines, power electronics, material science, and advanced manufacturing. We're a small, fast-moving team doing hard engineering that matters, and we're looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers alongside us.

About the role

H3X is looking to hire an embedded controls intern to support embedded controls & firmware development, as well as debugging across the entirety of the HPDM product line. This is not an ordinary internship. You will be given the full responsibility of an embedded controls engineer. The engineering team is intentionally small and operates at a very fast pace. A high degree of self-motivation and responsibility is required as you will be given significant freedom and have direct responsibility on relevant programs. We are focused on hiring Spring Interns, but will also have future Summer roles, and open to extended Co-Op periods.

What you will do:

- Assist in the development and maintenance of motor control firmware in C++, from low-level drivers to control algorithms

- Assist in the development and maintenance of motor simulations, configuration tools, and data processing scripts

- Collaborate with other teams to add support for new products and features

- Track down and resolve firmware bugs, and write firmware to help identify hardware bugs

- Support the testing team with custom testing builds, data collection, and troubleshooting

- Expand firmware testing and documentation, including unit tests, CI/CD pipelines, linting, and test plans

What we are looking for:

- Pursuing a Bachelor’s or graduate degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

- Proficiency in C++ and embedded systems

- Comfort with Python for scripting and tool development

- Comfort with the command line - running scripts, using git, and building projects

- Strong understanding of embedded systems fundamentals: microcontrollers, peripherals, real-time constraints, and hardware/software interface

- Hands-on, project-based experience with embedded systems

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills

- Motivated to know why and how something works, not just that it does

Nice to have experience:

- Motor control experience, understanding of fundamental motor equations

- Experience interfacing with power electronics or motor drive hardware

- Comfort with lab instruments and small hand tools

Why H3X

Joining H3X means working on hard, meaningful problems with a skunkworks-style team that's laser-focused on building exceptional products. We're deeply vertically integrated and have a very tight design-build-test loop, which lets us move from concept to hardware at unmatched speed. We've gone from idea to shipping product in less than two months.

We're a small, highly skilled team where everyone carries real responsibility and shares an extreme ownership mentality. We stay focused on the critical path, keep bureaucracy to a minimum, and structure everything around delivering results. You'll learn and grow faster here than you would anywhere else.

You'll work alongside world-class engineers and builders who are pioneering electric motor technology at scale on some of the coolest programs in the industry, from supersonic aircraft to power generation for AI datacenters. If you want your contributions to be visible and your work to directly shape American reindustrialization, you'll feel at home here.

Compensation & Benefits

- Salary/Hourly Compensation Range: $23 - $37/hr based on school level & experience

- Flexible hours (deliverable-based goals)

- Relocation package

- Monthly company events

- Friday Team Lunches

Our Values

Be Relentless Never give up, persevere until the job is done. Run toward problems, not away from them. Grit is key.

Gain insight through humility Approach every challenge with a learner’s mindset. Stay open to feedback, listen to others, and deepen your understanding through self-awareness. Put your ego aside and seek the truth in every discussion, especially when leading others.

Distill & Simplify Eliminate unjustified complexity and simplify wherever possible, whether in requirements, design, or execution. Use first principles thinking to distill every problem to its essence. Less is more.

Find your flow Engage fully and work with intention. Find the rhythm and deep focus that lets you do your best work. Discover your Ikigai - where your strengths, passions, and purpose meet and drive your personal fulfillment and team success. That is when the magic happens.

SEND (Solve, Evolve, Nail It, Deliver) Devise the best solution with the information at hand, test it, learn from it, and iterate quickly until you nail it. Nothing works perfectly the first time, but you should never hit the same issue twice. Stay laser-focused on solving customer problems and delivering solutions that create real value.

A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

Forward Deployed Software Engineers (FDSEs) work directly with customers to quickly understand their greatest problems and design and implement solutions to use data against them. Our customers rely on Palantir’s platforms for some of their most critical operations. As an FDSE working in our defense business, you will help defense customers plan and execute operations, understand their personnel and equipment footprint, and communicate in real-time with mission partners and legacy systems. You’ll have the opportunity to gain rare insight into and contribute to some of the world’s most critical challenges.

Core Responsibilities

As an FDSE Intern, your responsibilities look similar to those at a small startup, with the resources, stability and mentorship of an established tech company: You’ll work in small teams with minimal supervision and own end-to-end execution of high stakes projects. As an FDSE Defense Tech Intern, you will be supporting work specifically focusing on delivering our Palantir Defense capabilities to our most critical mission partners. Your day might span discussing architecture with fellow engineers, wrangling massive-scale data, coding a custom web app, speaking with customer contacts, or establishing strategy for your team.

FDSE Defense Tech Interns are treated just like full time engineers, with significant freedom and ownership over their work. Interns take responsibility for real world projects and outcomes that our customers rely on.

Our Principles:

- Impact: We address meaningful and exciting projects that change the world for the better.

- Ownership: We see projects through from beginning to end, working through any obstacles we may encounter. We trust each other to effectively handle time and priorities and give people the space to think for themselves.

- Collaboration: We work internally with people from a variety of backgrounds — such as other FDSEs, product teams, and Deployment Strategists. We also work externally with our customers, often on site, to understand and tackle their problems.

- Growth: We believe experiential learning is one of the best teachers and encourage ourselves and our peers to seek new challenges and opportunities for growth, as well as find new ways to innovate and share knowledge.

What We Value

- Willingness and interest to travel as needed to client sites. Ability to travel 25-50% preferred, but requirements vary by team and location.

- Ability to continuously learn, work independently, and make decisions with minimal direction.

- Ability to collaborate in teams of technical and non-technical individuals, and comfortable working in a constantly evolving environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users.

- An eagerness to creatively solve technical problems with data structures, storage systems, cloud infrastructure, front-end frameworks, and other technical tools.

- Interest in working with and using large scale data to solve valuable business problems.

What We Require

- Active US Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a US Security clearance prior to start of internship

- Engineering background, preferred in fields such as Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics, and Data Science.

- Proficiency with one or more programming languages, such as Python, Java, C++, TypeScript/JavaScript, or similar.

- Thoughtful responses to our application questions.

About Voltus

Voltus represents the “potential of us” to better manage energy through simple, cost- and risk-free demand response programs. Our commercial and industrial customers generate cash by allowing us to maximize the value of their operational flexibility in energy markets. We hire teammates who are bright, gritty, and good, and who have a genuine passion for delivering a cleaner energy future and for doing their best work in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.

The Role

This is not a general energy internship. You’ll join the Energy Markets team responsible for how Voltus positions and sells the capacity generated by its demand response portfolio across wholesale markets. These are high-stakes, high-consequence positions, and sharper quantification of risk directly improves the quality of the decisions we make.

Your mandate is to make those decisions sharper and more defensible. You’ll build the quantitative tooling and models that let us price the risk of any market decision and value it on a risk-weighted basis. You’ll help integrate this logic into our living data model.

If you’re energized by energy markets (especially capacity markets), probabilistic modeling, and trading risk, and you want to own a problem where your analysis directly shapes real market positioning decisions, read on.

Is This You?

This role blends quantitative rigor with energy markets, and it rewards people who like to build. You’ll likely enjoy it if:

- You like turning ambiguous problems into models and tools and owning them end to
end.

- You want to go deep on markets and risk, not stay at a high level.

- You’re motivated more by building things that last than by one-off analysis.

What You'll Do:

- Build scalable quantitative risk models and automated tooling to price and risk-weight capacity positions across auction-based and bilateral markets.

- Develop Monte Carlo, scenario, and stress-testing analyses that weight the full range of possible market outcomes and quantify upsides and downsides in uncertain scenarios.

- Research the long-term supply and demand drivers of capacity value in the markets we serve, including generation retirements and additions, load growth and data-center demand, virtual power plants, and evolving accreditation methodologies — and translate them into model inputs.

- Value and recommend risk-management strategies, including derivatives (for example, Black-Scholes-based valuation), hedging structures, and the option value of various market positions.

- Replace multi-source manual research with a data model that refreshes on the latest available data automatically.

What We're Looking For:

- Graduate-level candidate. You’re pursuing or have recently completed an MBA or a quantitative master’s degree, or you bring equivalent professional experience in trading, risk, or quantitative market analysis.

- Demonstrably quantitative. Probability and statistics are second nature, and you’re comfortable with probabilistic and statistical modeling, derivatives valuation, and core financial-risk concepts.

- Strong programmer. Proficient in Python, R, or MATLAB, plus SQL, Excel, and modern AI infrastructure and able to build tooling other people can rely on — not just one-off analyses.

- Demonstrated interest in capacity markets specifically. You can point to coursework, projects, work, or self-directed learning that shows real engagement with how power and capacity markets actually work, not just general enthusiasm for energy.

- Bright, gritty, and good. Intellectually curious, comfortable owning open-ended and ambiguous problems, and able to thrive in a remote, fast-paced environment. A track record of success working remotely is strongly preferred.

Bonus Points:

- Hands-on exposure to capacity, resource-adequacy, or ancillary-services markets in any ISO/RTO, demand response, or wholesale power trading.

- Experience turning analysis into durable tools, dashboards, or data pipelines.

- Familiarity with derivatives pricing and hedging in a commodity context.

Please note that at this time, we do not sponsor visas or transfers for new hires. Voltus teammates need to be authorized to work from their home location (in the US or Canada, unless otherwise indicated on the role description).

Additionally, while Voltus is an all-remote workplace, we have limitations on where employees are able to work for regulatory and security reasons. We expect that Voltans are working primarily from their home country. Working while traveling to other countries must be approved as per our Global Remote Travel Policy.

At Voltus, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer because we recognize that a diverse organization begins with a diverse candidate pool. This means we do not tolerate discrimination of any kind and are committed to providing equal employment opportunities regardless of your gender identity, race, nationality, religion, age, sexual orientation, veteran status, disability status, or marital status.

Please note: the pay for this role ranges from $20-$30/hour for undergraduate students and $30-$40/hour for graduate students.

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Launch & Scale Team

The Launch & Scale team builds the operating system that brings new sites, metros, and partners online and helps the network scale reliably. We turn complex dependencies into clear launch plans, readiness mechanisms, tools, and operating rhythms. We partner across infrastructure, permitting, flight operations, maintenance, commercial, partner readiness, and field operations. Our work stays close to real launches so that field lessons become repeatable systems rather than one-off fixes. As an intern, you will report to the Director, Launch & Site Operations and work closely with Launch Managers and cross-functional teams that bring the network online.

The Role

As the Launch & Scale Intern, you will contribute to a high-impact project that improves how Zipline plans, executes, and learns from launches. You will support Launch Managers by bringing structure to dependencies, analyzing readiness and performance, and helping teams turn field lessons into repeatable tools. You may spend time close to active launches, but you will work with experienced teammates rather than serve as the accountable launch owner. You will also own a clearly scoped project—such as a dashboard, process improvement, playbook, or lightweight automation—from problem definition through pilot and handoff. Along the way, you will receive coaching from the Director, Launch & Site Operations and collaborate with operators, engineers, commercial teammates, and field teams.

What You'll Do

- Support integrated launch plans for assigned workstreams by organizing milestones, dependencies, owners, risks, and open decisions.

- Analyze launch and site-operations data to identify bottlenecks, inconsistencies, and opportunities to improve speed, quality, or repeatability.

- Prepare materials for readiness reviews and operating forums, including concise status summaries, action logs, and decision briefs.

- Work with Launch Managers and functional teams to follow up on commitments, reconcile conflicting information, and surface blockers early.

- Build or improve practical tools such as dashboards, playbooks, templates, checklists, or lightweight automations.

- Participate in selected onsite launch activities, capture field observations, and translate lessons into process improvements.

- Own a scoped internship project from problem definition through pilot, measurement, and an accepted handoff to the team.

What You'll Bring

- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or graduate degree in operations, engineering, business, supply chain, data and analytics, or a related field.

- Structured problem-solving skills and curiosity about how complex physical or technical systems work.

- Comfort with quantitative analysis, including spreadsheets and at least one data or automation tool such as SQL, Python, or a business-intelligence platform.

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to make complex information easy to understand.

- Evidence of following through on a project involving multiple contributors through coursework, work, research, or extracurricular experience.

- Comfort operating in ambiguity, asking good questions, incorporating feedback, and staying reliable on details.

- Ability to work onsite in South San Francisco and willingness to travel occasionally within the United States to support launches.

Are you a dedicated problem-solver who is curious about algorithms for guided air vehicles? Are you interested in simulating highly complex physics problems and applying advanced data science to understand the results?

Would you like to learn about the newest and most innovative missile defense technologies?

The Weapon Systems Engineering group is seeking an intern to help us address complex engineering challenges for advanced missile defense systems. We are a team of experts whose goals are to conceive and assess real-world missile systems, perform laboratory / field testing, conduct in-depth analysis of post-processed data, and present findings to sponsors and the war-fighter.

- Assist in the development and efficient use of containerized software
- Use real world data to verify and validate complex models.
- Present key findings to various internal stakeholders and peers.
- Make an impact on processes and decisions on system design that keep our war-fighter safe!

Qualifications

You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you...

- Are pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Physics or Applied Math
- Have a passion for advanced computing, simulations, data analysis, and autonomous air vehicles.
- Proficiency in MATLAB and/or Python
- Demonstrated ability in developing, testing or troubleshooting software in a Linux environment
- Have a minimum 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale.
- Are able to obtain an Interim Secret level security clearance by your start date and can ultimately obtain a Secret level clearance. - Are proficient in another scientific computing language, such as SciPy, R, or Julia
- Have experience with a compiled and objected oriented language such as C++ or Java

- Have experience using a high-performance computing (HPC) cluster and job schedulers such as SLURM or UNIVA grid engine

As an Electrical/ Embedded Software Engineering Intern at Lexington Medical, you will work alongside our R&D engineers developing embedded systems for electromechanical surgical devices. - Collaborate with electrical, software, mechanical, and manufacturing engineers.

- Support engineering testing, verification, and technical documentation.

- Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related technical field.

- Coursework or project experience with embedded systems, electronics, microcontrollers, PCB design, firmware, or robotics.

- Experience programming in C or C++.

- Hands-on experience building, testing, or debugging hardware or embedded systems.

Advanced Quality

AQE interns work on engineering projects related to development of new products. Process Quality

PQE interns collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product sustainment. The Bioenergy Science and Technology (BEST) directorate within the National Renewable Energy Lab (NLR) performs a full range of research from exploring biomass at the molecular level through biorefinery process optimization to bring biofuels and bio-products to market. The Separations Science and Engineering Group focuses on developing and scaling separation technologies for a wide range of molecules, from bio-derived and chemically synthesized products, through to critical minerals including rare-earth elements from domestic waste feedstocks. Our goal is to improve process efficiency, selectivity, and techno-economic viability and our work is conducted in close collaboration with fermentation, catalysis, polymer synthesis, and techno-economic analysis teams. The group emphasizes translating fundamental separation science into practical, scalable solutions.

• electrochemical separations

• exposure to programming (e.g., python or rust) and support automation of custom separation systems

About The Opportunity

We are seeking a driven Robotic Systems Engineering Intern to help build, deploy, and support the automated technology powering Wonder’s restaurants. You will gain hands-on experience across the full robotic system—including mechanical hardware, electrical and controls systems, software, and system integration—while supporting multiple robot cell deployments, sustaining existing kitchen equipment, and contributing to the development of new automation initiatives currently in the conceptual phase.

The Impact You Will Make

- Support installation, commissioning, testing, validation, and operational launch of the Automated Expo robotic order-sorting platform across multiple restaurant deployments.

- Troubleshoot and resolve mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and system-integration issues in both development and live restaurant environments.

- Assist with prototyping, testing, and evaluation of new kitchen automation concepts, including researching unfamiliar technologies and helping assess potential solutions.

- Develop and improve deployment, commissioning, troubleshooting, and operational playbooks to make automation deployments more repeatable and scalable.

- Support sustaining engineering activities for Wonder’s back-of-house conveyance systems currently operating across nearly 150 locations, while partnering with cross-functional teams to improve reliability.

Tangible Requirements and Essential Job Duties

- Work hands-on with robotic and electromechanical systems, including motors, sensors, actuators, conveyors, 6-axis collaborative robot arms, and associated hardware and controls.

- Participate in integration, testing, commissioning, and troubleshooting activities at Wonder restaurant locations.

- Execute defined testing protocols, document results, identify issues, and work with engineering team members to determine appropriate solutions.

- Read and interpret technical documentation, component datasheets, mechanical drawings, electrical diagrams, and system-level documentation as needed.

- Use engineering judgment and structured problem-solving to investigate technical issues and help drive them through resolution.

- Collaborate with third-party vendors and internal engineering teams as needed to source components, troubleshoot equipment, and support system development.

Initial Focus and Key Deliverables (Post-Joining)

- Develop a strong understanding of the Automated Expo platform and its mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and operational interfaces.

- Support successful installation, commissioning, validation, and operational handoff of Automated Expo deployments.

- Build and maintain deployment and operational playbooks that improve consistency, troubleshooting, and scalability.

- Develop hands-on familiarity with Wonder’s existing kitchen conveyance systems and contribute to sustaining engineering and reliability improvements across the installed base.

- Support research, prototyping, testing, and early-stage development of new kitchen automation concepts.

Core Responsibilities

- Robotics & Automation: Support the development, deployment, and operation of robotic and automated food-service systems.

- Systems Integration: Work across mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and operational interfaces to help integrate and troubleshoot complete systems.

- Sustaining Engineering: Support troubleshooting and reliability improvements for automation systems operating in Wonder restaurants.

- New Automation Development: Contribute to research, prototyping, testing, and evaluation of emerging kitchen automation concepts.

- Deployment & Operational Readiness: Help prepare robotic systems for successful deployment and transition into reliable restaurant operations.

- Documentation & Scalability: Create and improve technical, deployment, and operational documentation to support repeatable execution.

What You Bring to the Table

- Currently pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related engineering field

- At least 2 years of relevant hands-on experience through internships, academic projects, robotics teams, maker projects, or other practical engineering experience.

- Demonstrated hands-on aptitude and enthusiasm for working with robotic, electromechanical, or automated systems.

- Foundational understanding of mechanical, electrical, controls, robotics, or related engineering principles.

- Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to investigate unfamiliar technical problems and develop practical solutions.

- Ability to read and understand mechanical drawings, electrical diagrams, technical documentation, and component datasheets.

- Experience with CAD, prototyping tools, low-voltage electrical wiring, basic programming, instrumentation, controls, or other engineering apparatus through coursework or hands-on projects.

- Strong communication, organization, and documentation skills, with a willingness to work collaboratively across engineering, restaurant operations, and vendor teams.

Job Description

The National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) is seeking two student interns to support its collaboration with the Kern Community College District’s California Renewable Energy Laboratory (CREL).

Interns will work with researchers in the Strategic Energy Analysis Center on applied research and educational activities related to carbon management, bio-based products, industrial energy systems, and large energy-load systems. The Strategic Energy Analysis Center (SEAC; www.nlr.gov/analysis) aims to increase understanding of energy policies, markets, resources, technologies, and infrastructure to address U.S. economic, security, and environmental priorities.

The two positions may support different combinations of research analysis, education, and curriculum-development activities. Specific project scopes will be determined in collaboration with the assigned NLR researchers based on project needs and the interns’ backgrounds and interests. Examples of potential work areas include:

Work Areas

- Biomass-derived intermediates and bio-based chemicals
- Carbon efficiency of bio-based conversion pathways
- Carbon utilization and low-carbon industrial systems
- Commercial and large energy-load systems
- Technical, economic, and environmental performance analysis
- Workforce and educational materials and activities related to energy systems

Research and Analysis

- Conduct literature reviews
- Collect and organize related technical, economic, and environmental data
- Compare and evaluate technology pathways using technical, economic, and environmental performance metrics
- Support spreadsheet analysis and technical documentation
- Summarize and present findings for researchers and project partners

Education and Curriculum Support

- Develop student-facing technical materials and case studies
- Prepare figures, presentations, and research summaries
- Adapt technical information for community-college audiences
- Support curriculum, workforce-development, and outreach activities

The internships will be fully remote, with regular virtual mentoring and team meetings. NLR will provide laptops and the required software and system access for remote work. No laboratory equipment or supplies will be required, as the work will focus on literature review, data analysis, spreadsheet-based analysis, and educational material development rather than laboratory experiments.

An optional visit to the NLR Golden Campus may be offered during the internship, subject to separate project funding, eligibility, scheduling, and NLR visitor requirements.

Cross-Functional Support

- Support ad hoc analysis requests tied to specific trading opportunities, contract structuring, or market events

About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Enterprise Systems Team

Joining Zipline as a Software Engineer Intern on the Enterprise Systems team, you will be part of the Application Software organization. You will take full ownership of the operational nervous system that powers everything from manufacturing and supply chain to inventory traceability and field deployment. This software is the critical infrastructure used daily by our technicians, planners, and manufacturing teams to ensure global production reliability. You will work directly with hardware and operations partners to lead technical designs and deploy high-availability services where correctness is vital for safety and aircraft throughput.

What You'll Do

- Drive core product domains. You will be the primary architect and owner for critical systems driving Manufacturing Execution, Supply Chain, Finance, Parts Traceability, and Inventory, ensuring their long-term technical health and strategic direction.

- Deliver measurable impact. Within your first year, you will stabilize essential services to 99.9% uptime, slash manual planning and production interventions by over 50%, and deploy a comprehensive traceability pipeline that tracks the vast majority of our manufactured assets.

- Lead technical design. You’ll define the APIs, data models, and service boundaries that power our operations, while prioritizing observability through metrics, SLAs, and robust runbooks.

- Bridge hardware and software. You will build resilient integrations between our digital services and physical hardware tooling, driving direct handoffs and ensuring our systems remain deterministic even during intermittent network connectivity.

- Own production excellence. Engineers participate in an on-call rotation to maintain high-availability services, leading incident response and driving continuous improvement through deep-dive postmortems.

- Embedded discovery. You’ll work directly on the shop floor with manufacturing, supply chain, and flight ops teams to prototype workflows and drive the adoption of new operational tools.

- Elevate the team. You will mentor peers and refine our CI/CD and automated testing practices to ensure that deployments remain safe and repeatable in our unique hardware-integrated environment.

What You'll Bring

- You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Masters and PhD students are also eligible.

- Product-minded engineering. You excel at understanding user needs, identifying root causes, and designing pragmatic solutions that balance business value with technical simplicity.

- Systems perspective. You break down ambiguous operational problems, collaborate with stakeholders to define the right solution, and deliver software that improves real-world processes.

- Strong technical fundamentals. You design maintainable systems, model data thoughtfully, make sound technical tradeoffs, and use AI effectively to accelerate development while maintaining high quality.

- Modern technology stack. You'll work across Python, Go, PostgreSQL, React, Kafka, gRPC, AWS, Grafana, and Honeycomb, using AI throughout the development lifecycle for design, implementation, testing, debugging, and code review. We value engineers who learn new tools quickly over experience with any specific technology.

- Operational excellence. You define meaningful service health metrics and reliability goals, create operational runbooks, participate in on-call rotations, and drive improvements through incident reviews.

- Quantifiable results. You have a track record of shipping high-impact features that reduce manual intervention and boost throughput, backed by concrete metrics like downtime reduction or significant time savings.

- Collaboration and discovery. This role requires regular on-site presence at our engineering or operations hubs to partner with cross-functional teams. When local, expect 5 days per week in-office, on the manufacturing floor, or at a test/commercial operations site. You are open to traveling up to 15% annually to be in close proximity to users and stakeholders.

- Owner’s mindset. You are a decisive engineer who balances velocity with absolute correctness. You understand the direct operational consequences of your code in a safety-critical, hardware-integrated environment.

Assuming this position, you will take full ownership of a mission-critical operational nervous system from day one. Your mandate involves delivering quantifiable results in system reliability and aircraft throughput within your first year, while managing SLO-driven services in close partnership with our physical hardware and field operations teams.

What Else You Should Know
